primary_claim: Tied SAEs are more resistant to feature absorption than untied SAEs when they have equal or more latents than true features (even under feature co-occurrence), but tied SAEs still learn 'broken latents' merging parent and child features under co-occurrence when the SAE is narrower than the number of true features — including in the extreme case of a single-latent SAE — showing that the core assumption behind Matryoshka SAEs (that a sufficiently narrow SAE perfectly represents the parent feature) is not strictly true.

effect.metric: cosine similarity of learned SAE latents to true toy-model features under varying latent/feature-count ratios and co-occurrence
effect.value: tied SAEs perfectly reconstruct true features when latent count >= feature count, even with co-occurrence; but produce broken/merged latents (partial cosine similarity mixing parent+child features) when the SAE is narrower than the number of true features, down to a single-latent SAE

contradicts_or_qualifies: Shows that the core assumption underlying Matryoshka SAEs (Bussmann/Leask/Nanda and Nabeshima, 2024) — that a sufficiently narrow SAE perfectly represents the parent feature in a parent-child relationship — is not strictly true; narrow SAEs instead learn broken latents merging parent and child features
stated_future_work: Prove what various SAE architectures will learn under different assumptions about underlying true features
Continue investigating whether smarter clustering of activations in latent activation histograms could help solve broken latents in real LLM SAEs
Combine Matryoshka SAEs with variations on the activation-orthogonality technique to project out child features from Matryoshka parent latents
Extend the activation-orthogonality technique to project out high-activating peaks (the inverse of the current approach) to fix broken latents in narrow/single-latent SAEs
limitations_stated: Struggled to get the activation-orthogonality technique to work well on real LLM SAEs
The toy settings in this post are not mathematical proofs, and conclusions about tied SAEs may not hold under all possible toy settings of feature co-occurrence
Not obvious that the highest-activating peak in a real SAE latent is actually the main feature the latent should track when there are multiple visible peaks
Activation distributions in real LLM SAE latents may have overlapping peaks that are not clearly separable, unlike in the toy examples
quote: The base assumption underlying why Matroyshka SAEs should solve absorption is not strictly true.
